spices and $70 in checked bag fees We spent $1,500 on logo and label design and we spent $600 on packaging for our spices and $750 for packing our spices into the jars plus a few other fees And in total we spent about $6,560 starting our Amazon FBA business In a little over eight years we made over $30 million in total sales across our business And since we launched on Amazon 5 years ago we've made over $1.4 million just by selling on Amazon In this video I'm going to share with you the step-by-step guide on how I started my business and how we grew it over the past eight years And at the still made over $34,000 in sales on Amazon in just the first year That was a big achievement and help set the stage for the massive spike in sales that we saw after our appearance on Shark Tank And stick around to the end of this video because the most valuable lesson is right at the end I'm going to share with you a mistake A mistake that cost my business $20,000 And this is a mistake that most new Amazon sellers make So if you're thinking of selling on Amazon or going on Shark Tank stay till the end of this video and avoid making this mistake yourself Now let me share with you a step-by-step guide on how I created this business My name is Ori and I started my first business when I was 16 years old I got a 3CD changer and started DJing parties In college I ran my own cap and gown rental business to help cut down the costs of graduating But after I graduated I moved to New York City and ended up working in advertising I was learning how the biggest companies reach their customers But I kept feeling the itch to be my own boss So I used some of my savings to start an ice cream cart with a close friend who had been working in restaurants It was a social enterprise that donated profits to support other street vendors But by the end of the summer we put the ice cream business on ice A few years later through some mutual friends I met a pair of entrepreneurs based in Europe who were working on a new kind of mortgage company and needed support They ended up giving me the initial investment money from my next company a Fintech company focusing on making the mortgage process in the US friendlier and more transparent Four years of running that company and after our series C financing fell through we were forced to sell the company and I was looking for my next thing That's right when my friend the same friend that I'd run the ice cream business with a few years ago had come back from overseas with an idea He had gotten his degree in international development and spent time as an aid worker in Afghanistan That's where he picked up a wild variety of cumin that he shared with some of his chef friends back in the US and they loved it and they kept asking when they could buy it and that was our light bulb moment People were buying single origin coffee and chocolate but nothing existed for spices And I knew that his background as a chef and aid worker and my experience in business and as an entrepreneur would be the perfect combination And with that we launched Burlap and Barrel a social enterprise sourcing single origin spices directly from smallh holder farmers all over the world After a few years of building up our supply chain selling doortodoor to restaurants enlisting the help of a packing facility and pitching our spices to journalists and home cooks all across the US to buy our spices on our e-commerce site we were ready to launch on Amazon 3 years after we started selling on Amazon we had the chance to appear on Shark Tank That had a big impact on our business overall but in particular we saw our Amazon sales skyrocket I'll share exactly how much money we made the night we were on Shark Tank in just a minute but make sure to like this video and to follow this channel Okay let's get into the step-by-step process for how we started our Amazon FBA business and how Shark Tank changed our Amazon business overnight When my business partner was working in Afghanistan he brought back a human that grows wild in the areas where he worked From there he was able to connect with other great spice farmers around the world a vertically integrated cardamom farmer in Guatemala and an organic spice cooperative in Zanzibar going cloves nutmeg and peppercorns We started small no market research no big expenses selling the spices that he had brought back out of his apartment and that helped validate our product idea Every dollar we made was invested back into buying more spices So if you're looking to find the perfect product to sell and you don't want to fly around the world here's a much easier option You can use Helium 10 Helium 10 is a research tool that can help you find your product idea So if you want to unlock all the premium features and help find your new product here's a link in the description with a discount code for Helium 10 Back to the business Our logo and our first batch of labels cost us around $1,500 We relied on our friends and family to get the business off the ground And my co-founder's cousin was a designer and we worked with her to design our logo and our initial labels We chose the name Burlap and Barrel because spices used to be transported in burlap sacks and in wooden barrels They went through dozens of versions of the logo ultimately choosing a version of hands woven together in the shape of a barrel To get your logo and packaging designed you can reach out to your cousin or you can use Fiverr Upwork or 99 designs And the way the 99 works is that you submit your design request and a bunch of designers send you their version of your logo or package and you choose one and just go from there On to packaging We spent about $1,450 on packaging to get things started on Amazon When we started the business we handpacked everything in pouches ourselves and wrote the name of the spice by hand We didn't have the budget for professionally printed labels so we turned that limitation into a strength We kept tweaking and iterating over time and eventually we were able to move into printed labels with barcodes metal lids embossed with our logo and a shrink band safety seal Many entrepreneurs make the mistake of spending too much money on packaging Luckily YouTube coach Travis has an in-depth tutorial that explains how you can get packaging done much cheaper in his Amazon FBA course The Passion Product Formula Link below in the description We spent about $1,570 on spices and transportation for our first production run for Amazon Those spices went into glass jars Since our spices were packed into glass each jar had to be packed into a protective outer box so that it wouldn't break And that cost us about $100 And then we closed the box with a printed Amazon barcode sticker For boxes and packaging you can find domestic sellers but as you scale up it'll make sense to look abroad There's Alibaba.com where there are hundreds of manufacturers across Asia Europe India You can also use thomasnet.com to find manufacturers that are exclusively in the US or you can buy directly through your co-packer or co-manufacturer if you use one For photography we spent $500 to get product photos taken and then we spent $200 to send those photos to an Amazon specialist to create more product images If you don't want to do all that work yourself there's a company called FBA Creatives that will do all your photos logo and packaging for you They'll even create your description and keywords too There's a link down in the description We spent about $1,000 to get set up as a public benefit corporation which is a legal structure that works well for social enterprises A standard LLC will cost you around $200 from wyregisteredagent.net And I recommend getting an LLC or limited liability company for your business because if you ever get sued or run into other trouble an LLC means that there's a separation between your business assets and your personal assets You can also get a DBA for $99 from Legal Zoom DBA means "doing business as" and it's the business name you use to operate under for tax purposes A DBA is great for marketing and branding but it won't offer you any legal protection Our next cost was spending $550 for a trademark So far we spent $6,070 and that was before getting the actual product That's a lot of money and I wasn't expecting it to cost so much Travis on YouTube says that there are 310 million Amazon customers worldwide and 230 million customers in the US alone So I knew this was a massive opportunity that was too good to miss Travis actually had a lot of great videos teaching Amazon FBA including a free 10-hour Amazon FBA course that's linked down below So my next cost was shipping Instead of paying for international shipping we were bringing spices back from overseas into America ourselves We're a bootstrap social enterprise so we've always needed to be very careful with how we spend our money We traveled to the spice farmers to meet them and carried back spices in our suitcases instead of hiring freight forwarders and customs brokers And we ended up coming ahead So from there we had to spend an additional $200 to ship our goods into the Amazon warehouse Typically if you're dealing with a standard overseas manufacturer there's a more streamlined process and there are two basic options Shipping via air is faster but it's much more expensive If you ship on sea on an ocean freight it'll be cheaper but it'll take much longer to arrive and typically you have to hit higher minimums in order to ship by sea Then it cost $250 to get our UPC codes UPC stands for "universal product code" and it's the barcode on the back of any product that gets scanned at checkout If you need just one you can go to gs1.org and buy one for $30 or you can get a pack of 10 for $250 And it cost $39.99 to set up my Amazon seller account An Amazon account fee is what you pay to be able to list and sell your products on Amazon So now we're ready to launch and I'm going to share with you how much we made in our first year in just a minute But so far we've spent over $6,560 to start this business Okay so here we are just about ready to launch and I'm definitely feeling nervous Travis had shared that Amazon is a $1.8 trillion company So I knew that we had a huge opportunity to find customers here So the year is 2020 and we had launched in July and made $34,544 in our first year on Amazon This was just half a year And it's important to know this was our revenue and not profits There are a lot of fees you need to pay on Amazon when you're selling In 2020 we spent $12,090 to make the product and paid $5,182 for the Amazon referral fee This is a 15% fee that you have to pay for the opportunity to sell on the Amazon platform The second fee was $11,745 for the Amazon FBA pick and pack fee FBA stands for "fulfilled by Amazon" which means that Amazon will pick pack and ship your product to your customers We didn't spend any money on PPC in our first year and I'll explain this in a second After all the expenses from my first year selling on Amazon we made $5,527 in net profit It felt great to make money but it was also very overwhelming And we just started listing on Amazon and we learned that it was more complicated than we thought Even basic things were not intuitive and we had a really hard time navigating the platform to get our listings up It was frustrating because it felt like a proper Amazon setup was out of reach We set ourselves up as FBM which is "fulfilled by merchants" and kept getting dinged since our systems weren't communicating well We even thought we might get kicked off of the platform But we added an Amazon consultant and they helped us finish our setup get more sophisticated on the platform and that helped us get going into our first full year in 2021 But we did make a big mistake with ordering a product that cost us $20,000 and I'll get to that in just a minute 2021 was our first full year selling on Amazon and we had about $86,000 in sales It cost us about $26,000 to make the product and $13,000 for the 15% Amazon referral fee $29,000 went back to Amazon FBA and that's their pick and pack fee And we also spent $7,700 for PPC advertising In 2021 our second year but really our first full year of selling on Amazon we made a $10,000 net profit This felt really encouraging We also learned that whenever we got a mention in a publication or any kind of press coverage we saw a blip in our Amazon sales We also started testing some light PPC PPC is "pay-per-click" where you can pay to have your listing at the top of the search results and you pay a small fee every time someone clicks on your listing Everyone needs a good coach and good resources to learn how to navigate Amazon That's where Travis comes in He teaches people how to start Amazon FBA businesses He's done over $7 million on Amazon and is sharing what he's learned There's a link below to sign up Fast forward to year three 2022 This was our biggest year yet We made almost $160,000 in sales on our third year And after all the expenses in our third year selling on Amazon we made $14,668 in net profit This was incredible Amazon was becoming a real channel for our small business We saw even more business pickup as we moved to FBA Most of our sales happen on our website but we want to be on Amazon to introduce our brand to the people who go shop on Amazon And we were optimistic that if we put more effort in that would result in more sales So we started adding spice sets to our lineup of single spices We started combining listings to get more reviews And we added more spices to Amazon to cross-sell and upsell and bundle all together Year four was 2023 2023 was the year that changed everything That was because this was when we appeared in Shark Tank We made $550,000 in sales in our fourth year And after taking out all of our expenses we actually ended up making $44,000 net We finally saw our Amazon business growing And this is a huge success because of Shark Tank We'd filmed the show back in September of 2022 and then we patiently waited for our air date When the show finally aired it was in April of 2023 at 9:00 p.m Eastern time We saw our sales jump from 9:00 p.m to midnight from what we had been doing previously of around $500 a day to almost $50,000 on the night the show aired The next day Saturday we saw $25,000 worth of sales And as things started selling out on Sunday we had $10,000 worth of sales on Amazon Then when all was said and done our orders settled down but to a level three to four times higher than our sales were before the show We had momentum that we were able to maintain since the show We also started working with a bigger agency now that we could afford their minimums and we saw a new level of sophistication and planning that let us keep growing The goal was to get under 16% TACoS an acronym that stands for "total advertising cost of sale" and that was done through a mix of careful advertising and pushing organic traffic affiliate traffic and PR traffic The success carried over into 2024 without counting November December we made $586,000 in revenue after all the expenses And in our fifth year of selling on Amazon we made almost $50,000 in net profits This was incredible We wanted to see if 2024 could match 2023 without a Shark Tank sized event promoting traffic And actually 2024 outpaced 2023 every single month other than April which was the month in 2023 when Shark Tank aired So in just over four years we've made $1.4 million in revenue on Amazon But remember revenue is not profit After taking out all of our expenses all of our advertising all the other fees we were left with $121,000 in profit A lot of this was because of hard work which led us having the opportunity to appear on Shark Tank which then helped us grow our Amazon presence immensely Amazon FBA can be a success even without Mr Wonderful And honestly we could have made so much more if we had avoided these three mistakes So pay attention Our first big mistake was number one discounting This mistake cost us about $5,000 We thought that discounting our product would help us get more sales but we found out that it lowers quality expectation and they don't come back when it's more expensive Big discounts attract a deal-seeking customer and that's not part of our model They didn't come back when the prices went back to normal So we kept the higher price and people see it as a premium product and that really works well for our business Our second mistake was over ordering This mistake cost us about $20,000 Bigger orders help save money and the savings from ordering more can be enticing but they also carry a really big risk Having too much inventory ties up your cash It costs money to keep your products stored in your warehouse and in Amazon's warehouses And it keeps you from investing in more profitable products and runs the risk of spoilage Even worse if you place a big order for your packaging and we've done it and you later find that typo or a barcode that doesn't scan it's really expensive to fix those mistakes After a few of those mistakes ourselves we ran sales We donated our extra inventory We got rid of our extra packaging But it was a really expensive lesson to learn Smaller orders allow us to iterate It might be more expensive per unit but we got to learn what our customers liked faster and we got to improve our product and packaging faster Our third mistake and this was our biggest mistake was really underestimating the customer I think this mistake cost us at least $50,000 This was a big mistake that took us about seven years to figure out We really thought that our customers were only interested in small packages of spices Maybe they were buying a single spice or maybe three spices or six spices But when we looked at our site and our data we saw that some customers were placing bigger orders really big orders So we tested bigger pack sizes We now have packs of 12 spices 24 spices and even a pack of 60 spices That's our complete collection We found that bigger spice sets are really popular especially when someone is shopping for a gift which is often done with a budget in mind We also make higher margins off of these gift sets And we've all been there buying a lastminute gift for someone Amazon does a really good job delivering exactly on time So if you don't make it easy for your customers to find an options that matches their budget and that can deliver on time they're going to look elsewhere and buy something else for their gifting This was a mistake that was not in terms of cost of money that we spent but in terms of missed revenue So don't miss out on your biggest spenders because you don't offer bigger sets Overall Amazon has helped our business reach a massive new audience And then Shark Tank blew our sales out of the water and we found that our sales were able to not only keep up but even outpace Shark Tank the next year We built a really healthy e-commerce business without taking on investors and you can do it too One really important key was getting the right experts to help guide you along the way that can make a huge impact on your success So make sure that you check out Travis's Amazon FBA program The Passion Product Formula There's a link in the description for you to join or just get started with his free 10-hour Amazon FBA course Thank you for tuning in That's all for me goodluck on Amazon!
